skill.description: 国土地理院の公開API(認証不要)で、住所から緯度経度、緯度経度から標高、緯度経度から住所(市区町村+町丁目)を引く。住所検索は曖昧一致で件数が多く、先頭が正解とは限らない点まで扱う。地図の描画・経路・郵便番号検索は対象外(郵便番号はzipcode-lookup、住所の正規化はaddress-normalize)。
skill.summary: Look up Japanese address coordinates, ground elevation, and municipality names using public GSI services without an API key.

content.user_title: Look Up Japanese Coordinates, Addresses, and Elevation
content.value_statement: Japanese location lookups can return ambiguous matches or missing data without an HTTP error. This skill uses public GSI services to retrieve coordinates, elevation, and municipality names with explicit result handling.
actual_capabilities: Search Japanese addresses and facility names for latitude and longitude using the public GSI address-search API.
Prioritize normalized prefix matches and report total candidates, returned candidates, and ambiguity warnings.
Retrieve ground elevation in meters and the source label, while recognizing the missing-data marker.
Resolve coordinates to prefecture, municipality, and town or block using reverse geocoding and the GSI municipality table.
Handle leading-zero municipality codes and normalize full-width characters during candidate comparison.
Run a Python command-line helper using only standard-library modules, without API keys or account registration.
limitations: Live lookups require internet access and send supplied addresses or coordinates to GSI services, whose availability can change.
Coordinates represent address reference points; reverse results lack full street numbers, and elevation excludes building height.
Map rendering, routing, postal-code lookup, comprehensive address normalization, and survey or legal certification are outside scope.
Searches can return ambiguous matches or missing data; the output limit does not reduce the full response download.

use_cases.description: Retrieve ground elevation and its source label for a known Japanese coordinate, while identifying unavailable data.

prompt_templates.title: Check Ground Elevation
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up ground elevation at latitude [latitude] and longitude [longitude]. Include the source label and report unavailable data without guessing.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Recorded Location
prompt_templates.prompt: Reverse-geocode latitude [latitude] and longitude [longitude]. Resolve the municipality code and report prefecture, municipality, town, and available address precision.

prompt_templates.prompt: Search GSI for [facility name], showing up to [count] candidates. Compare normalized prefix matches and municipalities; request clarification before selecting an ambiguous result.

best_practices: Use specific addresses with prefecture and municipality names; review ambiguous candidates instead of assuming the first match is correct.
Verify latitude and longitude order, preserve missing-data notices, and state that coordinates and elevations are approximate reference information.
Attribute GSI, avoid rapid bulk requests, and confirm permission before sending sensitive location data to an external service.
anti_patterns: Automatically selecting the first fuzzy match without checking its municipality or title.
Treating HTTP success as proof of valid elevation or inventing an address when reverse geocoding returns no data.
Using broad queries repeatedly or assuming the display limit bounds downloaded data.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The documented GSI services require neither authentication nor registration.

faq.question: What software does the helper require?
faq.answer: The command-line helper requires Python 3 and internet access. It uses standard-library modules without additional packages.

faq.question: Can this skill look up postal codes or routes?
faq.answer: No. Postal-code lookup, routing, and map rendering are outside its scope.

faq.question: Why is the first address candidate sometimes incorrect?
faq.answer: GSI address search uses fuzzy matching without relevance ordering. The helper prioritizes normalized prefix matches, but you must still verify candidates.

faq.question: What happens when location data is unavailable?
faq.answer: The helper reports missing elevation or an unavailable reverse address. The service does not reliably distinguish unsupported locations from invalid input.

faq.question: Are these results suitable for surveying or legal evidence?
faq.answer: No. Coordinates are representative points, and elevation describes ground level. The skill documentation excludes survey and legal use.
